name: Avenable
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Avenable is an Arthurian heroine. This ambitious and vital young British woman was not satisfied with her options at home. She dressed herself as a young man and renamed herself Grisandole. She left for adventure and found work in Rome. The emperor made her seneschal, or steward, so she became one of his closest confidants. She heard him complain about a haunting dream. In the dream a pig was crowned with jewels. The dream told him that only a wild man could interpret it. Avenable went to find the wild man. He was none other than the great magician Merlin, who lived in the woods during a period of madness. Merlin did interpret the dream. Rome's empress was in fact a pig engaged in shapeshifting. Her offspring were not really knights but piglets. In horror the emperor had the empress killed. Once Avenable revealed her true gender, the emperor married her.

okr.objective: This article recounts the tale of the Arthurian heroine Avenable, who disguised herself as a man, solved the emperor's dream with Merlin's help, and married the emperor.
key_results: She dressed as a young man and renamed herself Grisandole.
She served as seneschal to the emperor in Rome.
She found the wild man Merlin in the woods.
The emperor killed the empress after she was revealed as a pig.
